Read `README.md` and current rollout evidence first. Produce exactly one multi-wake target-policy candidate in `solver/`. Keep candidate-specific reasoning in `logs/optimize/wake_policy_notes.md`, and add or materially revise at least one evidence-backed reusable lesson in `guidance/control_experience.md` from the assigned parent, sampled solver results, and inherited logs. If no positive lesson survives the evidence, record a concrete negative result and what later workers should avoid or test. The candidate is incomplete until both files are updated. Work only inside this Phase 2 workspace.

This is the no-Bookshelf ablation: no cross-domain fish-control research shelf
is provided. Base controller proposals only on the task contract, current and
inherited guidance, sampled solver results, inherited optimizer logs, and
current rollout evidence. Do not search for or reconstruct the omitted shelf
from neighboring configurations or repository history.

I’m using the `read-wake-visual-signals-first` skill because this policy change is driven by multi-wake rollout evidence. I’ll first read the workspace contract, then follow the skill’s visual-inspection workflow before touching the candidate or guidance.

The evidence set contains four current rollouts and inherited optimizer logs. I’m anchoring the comparison on the strongest finite rollout (`solver_89ae…`) and using the prefilled rollout plus the positive-sign predecessor as contrasting failures; next I’m matching their visible paths to trajectory, load, saturation, and policy differences.

The inherited record sharpens the question: additive bearing-rate damping failed, and the newest direct heading-rate damper improved scalar progress but still exited earlier than the undamped anchor while raising loads. I’m now inspecting the common prewarm and released sheets to decide whether that gain came from useful wake entry or simply a faster version of the same upper-loop failure.

The current sheets show that heading-rate feedback changed the approach usefully—it drove roughly twice the upstream mean speed—but did not change the failure topology: the fish still builds lateral drift, hits the posterior/rate/command caps, curls upward, and exits sooner. An inherited “closing-only” bearing brake is an important boundary because it instead lost all upstream authority; I’m checking that sheet before recording the candidate hypothesis.

The visual-first skill has now completed its required evidence pass. It steers the candidate toward retaining the evaluated heading-rate mechanism that produced the strongest upstream motion, while adding only a small bounded body-lateral-velocity term to address the remaining upper-boundary drift; the inherited 65% closing brake shows why this new correction must not broadly suppress geometric steering.

The candidate and durable lesson are now updated. I’m at the contract-verification stage: schema ownership, Julia materialization, editable-boundary checks, and the mandated assigned-parent guidance comparison. No CFD will be run.
